about.title: Ripon Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Ripon is a small, tight-knit community, but that doesn't mean property owners get a pass when someone gets hurt on their premises. Whether the fall happened in a store parking lot near SR-99, on a wet floor at a local restaurant, or on a broken stair at an apartment complex off N Jack Tone Road, California law requires owners to keep their property reasonably safe and to fix or warn about hazards they knew or should have known about. These claims often come down to details: how long a spill sat unattended, whether a warning sign was posted, and what surveillance footage shows. LawProactive doesn't practice law, but we connect injured Ripon residents with independent attorneys who understand how to investigate these cases and preserve evidence before it disappears. There's no cost to get connected, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless they recover money for you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Fall

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Investigation
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can dig into maintenance logs, complaint histories, and inspection records to build that case.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Ripon businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having nothing.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present your side clearly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Ripon?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If your fall happened on property owned by a government entity, such as a city building or public sidewalk, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. It's best to talk to an attorney as soon as possible so no deadline gets missed.

items.question: What if I fell on a wet floor with no warning sign in a Ripon store?
items.answer: The absence of a warning sign can support your case, but you still need to show the owner knew or should have known about the wet floor. Photos of the scene, witness names, and any incident report filed with the store can all help establish this. An attorney connected through LawProactive can help gather that evidence.

items.question: Does it matter that Ripon is a small town with fewer big retailers?
items.answer: Not really — premises liability law applies the same whether the fall happened at a national chain or a family-owned shop near W Main Street. What matters is whether the property owner failed to address a known hazard, not the size of the business. Smaller businesses may have less formal record-keeping, which makes fast evidence gathering even more important.
